stories.title: Agents log six hours per human hour, so reading time needs a budget like page load
stories.blurb: Patrick Neeman works through Anthropic's own study of how agents changed its work: sessions idle 80 percent of the time waiting for a person, and reading all output would take more than half the week even for non-coders. His seven steps are old UX material applied to a new sender: set a reading budget per workflow, make agents justify a severity level so routine requests stay in a digest, show what changed next to what existed in review, and write decisions where agents can read them.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: Human attention is the new old bottleneck. We have to design for it even more.
sources.author: Patrick Neeman

stories.title: CSS random() lands in Safari and Chrome, and Smashing asks where a design system can afford imperfection
stories.blurb: Brecht De Ruyte builds demos with the new native function, from slightly tilted type to splayed cards and a punk fanzine, with no JavaScript or Sass loops generating hundreds of static rules. The syntax is a min, max and optional step in matching units. His argument for design-system people: pixel-perfect grids, and the sameness of unguided LLM layouts, make interfaces sterile, and a few degrees of controlled chaos read as handmade.

sources.name: Smashing Magazine
sources.headline: Embracing Playful Imperfection With The CSS `random()` Function

stories.title: The Body Shop promotes the Pod from supporting device to the organising principle of its packaging
stories.blurb: Together Design London rebuilt the Body Butter and Bath & Body range around a graphic asset from the brand's own history, set on the heritage green of Anita Roddick's first Brighton store, with Sally Caulwell's ingredient illustrations inside it giving each product its own personality. The case is about scale: one silhouette that stays recognisable across a large portfolio of formats and names, with individuality handled inside the shape rather than by changing it.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: The Body Shop returns the Pod to its packaging

stories.title: Twinnin's rebrand turns face-mapping coordinates and hologram tints into a Verified Human mark
stories.blurb: UnitedUs reduced the consent registry for faces to four words, "Your face. Your control.", and two badges, Licence and Defend, with the logo built from facial-recognition points and finished in the security-label holography of DVDs and game cartridges. Every person in the imagery is a verified user. A clear example of a brand borrowing visual codes of protection to explain a product people have not needed before.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Can a trust mark keep your face out of AI? UnitedUs thinks so with its rebrand for Twinnin

stories.title: Bud Rodecker: a rebrand measured on launch day is the wrong test, measure whether it is still in use a decade later
stories.blurb: The Span partner takes HBO Max and Jaguar as cases of brands treating equity as disposable, and sets against them institutions he designs for, where an identity has to absorb new stories for decades without losing recognition. The useful part is the closing list: build on principles not trends, design systems not artefacts, leave room for evolution, prioritise clarity over novelty, invest in typography and proportion over gimmicks, and balance consistency with relevance.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Does brand design have a longevity problem?

stories.title: Idaho's anti-drug campaign shows no drugs: sixteen uncut moments, one line of copy, local shooters
stories.blurb: Drake Cooper's spots are single-shot fifteen-second clips of everyday life, pizza night, a summit with friends, a baby laughing, with "This is an anti-drug ad" appearing midway and fading again. No spokesperson, no logo sign-off. The production model is as transferable as the idea: one brief and one rule to fourteen filmmakers across the state, clips licensed from nine, six weeks from brief to air.

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: Idaho Is Already the Best Anti-Drug Ad

stories.title: Laurenz Brunner's Dictionary of the Illegible argues that illegible is not the same as unreadable
stories.blurb: The Source Type book collects metal band logos, grawlixes, emoji codes and messages built to slip past online censors, and reads them as typography that communicates by exclusion and texture. In the interview Brunner refuses the good-versus-bad typography distinction: what looks dysfunctional in one context carries meaning in another, and writing has stayed tied to semantic logic long after art embraced abstraction.

sources.name: It's Nice That
sources.headline: Source Type's Dictionary of the Illegible explores what happens when typography stops making sense

stories.title: Boltgun 2's retro pixels are 3D models shot from eight angles and flattened into sprite sheets
stories.blurb: Lead artist Mark Chambers explains that the sprites carry normal, ambient occlusion and emission data and are projected onto billboarded planes, so the surface stays crisp and uniformly spaced while modern lighting runs underneath. The craft lesson is the limit they chose to keep: silhouettes that read instantly at speed, with the Warhammer detail squeezed into them rather than rendered.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2's lead artist reveals how they made pixel art feel authentically retro

stories.title: October's agency moves: strategy heads everywhere, no 'AI specialist' in any release, and measurement written into briefs
stories.blurb: Creative Boom's monthly roundup reads four new strategy leads at Landor, Small World, Dalziel & Pow and FutureBrand as agencies doubling down on what AI cannot do, while ustwo puts a former creative director in charge of tech and Brandtech hires Chris Garbutt to show AI-first and craft can coexist. Second pattern: proof, with Interbrand appointing a brand economist and Reebok's agency win announced with an engagement rate. Third: consolidation in Manchester, York and the US.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Booms Shakes: October s strategy power moves, Manchester mergers, and why craft is the word of the month

stories.title: Figma adds 20 MCP partners while Dylan Field calls the protocol imperfect and tilted toward frontier labs
stories.blurb: At Config India Figma announced partners including Linear, Notion, ClickUp, Mistral and Meta Muse, days after a public exchange in which Field asked why Anthropic does not expose its own artifacts via MCP. His stated reason for not opening Figma data fully: the more exposed through MCP, the higher the chance of abuse. For teams building agent workflows on design files, the limit is policy, not technology.

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.headline: Figma co-founder Dylan Field thinks MCP is not a perfect protocol

stories.title: Claude Desktop's Code tab replaces VS Code for non-engineers, and Cowork is not the same thing
stories.blurb: Paweł Huryn's guide for product people maps what used to need an IDE onto the new desktop app: folders with project instructions and skills, a permission mode, model and effort choice, app previews. His test is the comparison with Cowork, which runs in a limited virtual machine, cannot preview apps or hold project-specific skills and does not read AGENTS.md. Worth it for designers who prototype with Claude Code and want to skip the terminal.

sources.name: The Product Compass
sources.headline: Claude Desktop v2.0: You Don't Need VS Code Anymore!
sources.author: Paweł Huryn
